statement:
These are the licence, copying, notice and authors files of the sources Bun pins for its runtime: the libraries it vendors, WebKit's JavaScriptCore, WTF and bmalloc, ICU, the Rust standard library and crates, the npm packages it embeds as Node.js polyfills, and the GCC static C++ runtime, together with the licences of projects Bun ports code from. Where a source keeps its licence statement in the comments of its files, those comments are included as they are; the files searched that way and what that search leaves out are listed under Known gaps.
They were collected from the exact sources Bun's recipes pin, not read out of the executables. They show what Bun is built from, not which files a given executable contains. What could not be established is listed under Known gaps at the end.

gaps.text: Which of these sources ended up in the executables is not measured. The executables are stripped, Bun's per-file source lists were not evaluated, and the static archives' linked objects cannot be told apart, so every text here belongs to a source candidate, not to proven content.

Bun links JavaScriptCore, WTF, bmalloc and ICU from a prebuilt WebKit release asset (bun-webkit-linux-arm64-lto, release autobuild-d6375c72affe0f70222cdcb45012b10f0bf3a9d5), which Bun pins only by tag name. The asset served on 17 November 2026 (sha256 78d840c6afda98bebf6036f53f3227a7149514206bfdb60f384fb85a2e8dd212) contains no licence files, so the texts here come from the pinned WebKit and ICU sources. Nothing shows that this asset is the one the release was built with.

JavaScriptCore and WTF source files carry their own BSD or LGPL headers with per-file copyright lines. Those headers are not reproduced here; JavaScriptCore's COPYING.LIB and the third-party licence files of JavaScriptCore and WTF are.

Licence statements in source comments were searched only in Bun's runtime sources (src/, packages/bun-usockets/, packages/bun-uws/: every run of comments with a licence grant), libarchive's libarchive/, Rust's libm sources, picohttpparser and bmalloc with libpas (each file's leading comment and every later comment with a grant). Comments were recognised by the comment syntax the rules assign to each file type. The per-file comments of the other vendored libraries, of JavaScriptCore and WTF, of ICU, of the crates and of the polyfill packages were not searched; their licence files are included. Files in the searched scope that still mention copyright outside the printed comments are listed in their own gaps below.

Bun's recipes pin the GCC archive by sha256 and link with -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc, and the executables name GCC 13.1.0-8ubuntu1~20.04.2. Nothing shows that this release was linked against that exact archive.
The gcc-13 copyright file refers to the full GNU GPL version 3 at /usr/share/common-licenses/GPL-3 instead of including it.

The gcc-13 copyright file also refers to full texts it does not include: GPL version 2 (the D front end), the Artistic licence and GPL version 1 (the DMD compiler), the LGPL (newlib) and the GFDL 1.2 (documentation). They concern parts of GCC other than libstdc++ and libgcc and are not included.

Bun's LICENSE.md names code ported from other projects without pinning the upstream revisions. For @eslint/json, @eslint/markdown, ESLint, typescript-eslint, the ESLint plugins, oxc, tsgolint, Prettier, typescript-go and the import sorting plugin, the licence and NOTICE texts Bun keeps beside the test cases it took from them are included above, as Bun's copies at the pinned revision; whether they are the texts of the revisions that were ported is not established. For the other projects that table names (among them esbuild, simdutf, libbase64, uucode, uWebSockets, Tigerbeetle, esquery, V8, Biome, postcss and Svelte), Bun's tree has no licence file, and none is included except where the ported source keeps its licence in its comments.

The Rust crates are those Cargo.lock reaches from Bun's workspace, leaving out dev-dependencies. Features, target conditions, build scripts and procedural macros were not resolved, so the list is a superset, and the executables keep no paths that would show which crates were linked.
The Node.js polyfill packages are every package in Bun's node-fallbacks lockfile. Their bundled output was not matched against the executables.

Bun's src/js/internal/fs/glob.ts embeds Node.js v26.3.0's minimatch bundle, which also contains balanced-match and brace-expansion. The source labels the bundle ISC without reproducing its full licence text. The three projects' corresponding licence texts have not been pinned and packaged here; the grant detector does not establish coverage from a bare licence name.
